observations.seen: Frame 1's far floor section is blown out to near-white, and the treasure chest on it reads as a translucent yellow ghost. Ceiling strip lights glow but cast little shaped falloff onto walls.
No visible cast shadows from the chest, crates, round hatch box, or viewmodels. Wall-floor and wall-ceiling junctions lack contact darkening or AO, so geometry looks pasted together.
Frame 4 shows faint sheen on the concrete floor. Otherwise surfaces show no environment reflections, and the frame 3 water plane is a flat teal slab with no reflection or refraction.

The levels are long box corridors with repeated rails and yellow floor stripes. The flooded area in frame 3 is a hard-edged rectangle sunk into the floor, and the frame 1 ceiling has a dark, stretched, blotchy texture.
Frame 2 has teal haze, glowing orbs, and sparkle particles that add mood, but the haze washes the near-camera rifle to grey-white instead of sitting in depth.
The floor texture in frames 3 and 4 is low resolution and smeared. Wall stone and concrete tile visibly. The 'B-4 OFFICERS ONLY' decal in frame 4 runs sideways and is unreadable.
The machine gun viewmodel has faceted low-poly shading with hard normals. Doors and the hatch box are flat textured cubes.
Corridors center a vanishing point, but long empty walls and a bare foreground floor (frame 3) leave much of each frame with nothing to read.

In frames 3 and 4 the pistol floats mid-right at small scale, detached from the bottom edge, so it reads as an object in the world rather than a held weapon. Viewmodel placement is inconsistent with frames 1 and 2.
Bloom and exposure clip the frame 1 floor and the frame 2 rifle. A mild grey grain/haze flattens contrast in frames 3 and 4.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
